question_text: What is the difference between feature extraction and fine-tuning in transfer learning, and why freeze the base first?
correct_answer: In feature extraction, the entire pretrained convolutional base is frozen and used strictly to generate representations, while only a newly attached dense classifier head is trained on top. In fine-tuning, the top few layers of the convolutional base are unfrozen and trained jointly with the classifier using a very low learning rate. Freezing the base first is critical because the new classifier has random initial weights; backpropagating their massive initial errors would destroy the delicate, pretrained visual representations in the base.
